name: Art Deco dance shoe
summary: The strap shoe of the Jazz Age. It has a T-strap or a bar strap over the instep and a Louis or Cuban heel. It uses satin, kid or metallic leather with a cut-out or beaded pattern.

philosophy.core_thesis: A dancing woman needs a shoe that stays on the foot, so the strap holds the instep and the Deco pattern shows in every step.
design_principles: Fasten the shoe with a T-strap or a bar strap over the instep; fix it with a button or a small buckle.
Set the heel at 5 to 7 cm, curved in a Louis or a Cuban shape.
Round the toe, and cut the vamp low so that the instep shows.
Cut a geometric pattern in the vamp: a sunburst, a chevron or a step.
Cover the shoe in satin, in kid, or in a metallic leather that catches the light.
Match the shoe to the dress in colour; dye the satin to a sample of the cloth.
Use a thin leather sole that slides on the floor.
anti_patterns: A thick rubber sole that grips the floor
A bare, strapless slip-on court shoe
A pastel and floral Victorian pattern
A platform or a stiletto heel

silhouette.shape: A low, light shoe with a round toe, a strap across the instep and a curved heel.
silhouette.line: A graphic line: the strap crosses the vamp at a right angle to the foot.
silhouette.fit: Close at the heel and held at the instep by the strap, so that the foot can move freely.
silhouette.proportion: Heel 5 to 7 cm; strap width 1 to 2 cm; vamp cut short, about one third of the foot.
rules: Cross the instep with one strap or two straps, and fix it at the side.
Cut the pattern in a repeated geometric form.
Keep the sole thin and the heel curved.
Match the metal of the buckle to the dress.

fabrics.rule: Use kid for day dances and satin or brocade for the evening. Add a metallic, snake or patent trim, and keep the sole in thin leather.

construction.closures: A bar strap or a T-strap with a button or a small buckle on the outside.
construction.details: A cut-out pattern, a rhinestone or a bead trim on the vamp, a metal buckle, a contrast heel and a kid lining.

surface.pattern: Geometric and flat: a sunburst, a chevron or stepped lines in two colours.
surface.gloss: Satin at 40–60 GU; patent and gilded leather at 70–95 GU.
surface.wear: The shoe looks best new and bright; a scuffed or faded satin shoe loses its effect.

palette.strategy: Gold, silver and black with one colour for the dress; a second metal on the buckle.

making.scale: Made to order by a custom shoemaker for the client, with a ready-made line for the shop.
making.signs: An even pattern cut, close beading, a firm strap and a smooth heel curve.

emotion.target_response: A sense of glamour and speed: a bright shoe that moves with the music.

an Art Deco evening shoe line
a museum label for a 1920s shoe
avoid_when: the brief wants a flat or sports shoe
the brief wants a stiletto or platform
the brief is a 1960s youth look

modifiers.how: Drop the strap, lengthen the toe to a point, and thin the heel to a steel-cored spike.
Add a 5 cm platform under the sole, raise the heel to 12 cm, and brighten the colour.
